resources.string: Streams NZB releases from your NNTP providers. Runs as a separate program on this device; its third-party notices are bundled with the app.
Search your own Newznab indexers and play NZBs with your NNTP providers
Find NZBs and play them directly with your providers. Credentials stay on this device, in this profile.

Nuvio connects to your indexers and Usenet providers directly from this device, with your own accounts. Nothing goes through a Nuvio or shared server.

• Your indexers and providers see this device’s IP address, like any other app you use.
• API keys and logins stay on this device, in this profile.
• Every search uses API hits on each enabled indexer. For indexers with low limits, give them a lower priority and turn on Search lower priorities only as fallback.
• Each indexer and provider still applies its own rules and limits.
Add and enable at least one provider and one indexer to search.
Could not load or save Usenet sources. Check device storage and try again.
Enter the indexer URL; the API path (usually /api) is added to it. Supports Newznab and compatible Prowlarr or NZBHydra endpoints.
Remove this source and its saved credentials from this profile?
Providers with the same priority share traffic. Lower priorities are only used for articles the higher ones are missing.

Priority orders your indexers. It decides which copy of a repeated release is kept when Hide repeated releases is on, and which indexers are searched first when Search lower priorities only as fallback is on.
Results fetched per query from this indexer before filtering. Unlimited reads every available page and can take longer and use more API requests.
Could not connect. Check the host, port and TLS setting.
Secure connection failed. Check the TLS setting and port (usually 563 with TLS, 119 without).
Sign-in failed. Check the username and password.
The provider refused the connection. It may have reached its connection limit, or the account may be inactive.
This is a local network address. Enable Allow self-hosted servers to use it.
Check the name, host, port (1–65535), credentials and connections (1–4096).
Enter a name, a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL and an API path such as /api.
Could not connect. Check the API URL, key and indexer limits.
Last request failed: API key rejected
Last request failed: could not reach the indexer
%1$d API hits left, %2$d grabs left (as of %3$s)
Sort by the order chosen below.
Quality tiers and trusted release groups, with a preference for movies under 30 GB and episodes under 5 GB. Larger releases remain available.
Prioritize remuxes, high-quality encodes and trusted release groups. 1080p remuxes rank above 4K WEB-DL. No preferred size ceiling.
Prefer 1080p WEB releases and efficient codecs, with movies under 12 GB and episodes under 2 GB. Keep larger alternatives below.
Prefer 1080p and 720p releases without HDR or Dolby Vision labels, with a boost for AVC video and AAC or Dolby Digital Plus audio. Keep other formats as alternatives.
Prefer releases labelled with this audio language before quality and size. Other and unlabelled releases remain available.
Total results shown across all indexers after filtering and sorting.
Results fetched per query unless an indexer overrides this setting. Each page costs an API request.
Exclude CAM, telesync and screener releases
Exclude full Blu-ray and DVD discs
Hide whole disc releases. A Blu-ray disc plays from its feature clip; a DVD disc does not play. Remuxes of a disc always show.
Search lower priorities only as fallback
Off: every indexer is searched. On: lower-priority indexers are only searched when the higher ones find nothing, which saves API hits.
Show a release found by several indexers once, from the indexer with the highest priority.
Show the release name of each result above its size, age and indexer.
Show results as each indexer answers
Off: the list appears once every indexer answered, or after 5 seconds if one is slow, and fills in from there. On: it grows and reorders as each indexer answers.
Releases labelled AVAILABLE played recently with your providers, here or in another episode of the same pack. On: they are listed first whatever the sort. Off: they keep their place.
Memory and streaming presets. Changes apply to the next stream.
Limits the combined connections of your providers. Automatic uses each provider’s allowance.
Prepare the video’s beginning and seek index together. Uses a little extra bandwidth and memory. Applies to the next stream.
Request compressed NZB metadata to reduce startup latency. Applies to the next stream.
Keep downloaded NZBs for 14 days, up to 256 MiB, so playing a release again does not grab it again. Turning this off clears the cache.
Allow NZB and provider addresses on your local network or this device. Enable only for trusted addons and self-hosted services. Applies to the next stream.
Try to continue through small gaps in a damaged video. Missing content may cause picture or audio glitches, and some videos may still fail. Applies to the next stream.
%1$s: indexer search failed. Check the API URL, key and limits.
The Usenet stream could not be opened: %1$s
This release is missing parts on your Usenet provider (removed or incomplete upload). Try a different release.
Parts of this release are damaged on your Usenet provider, or packed in a way that cannot be streamed. Try a different release.
Your Usenet provider refused the login. Check the provider’s username and password in the Usenet settings.
Your Usenet provider’s download quota is used up. Check your account with the provider.
This release has no real video in it. Try a different release.
